| [CLAIM-600](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-600.md) v4 | Transient support can be withdrawn safely when it starts a process that keeps itself going on a flux that will stay available, when it is large enough to carry the supported party past any threshold that process has, when the threat it stood in for has gone, and when the party could do the work and did it throughout, in each subtask it must later do alone and not only in its role as a whole, at no more effort than it could bear, and, where the capacity is cumulative and its field moves fast, kept doing it after withdrawal; inputs the party cannot produce must stay supplied as a standing part of the arrangement, support that fails these leaves dependence or decay, and persistence after withdrawal is needed to tell which, though slow reversion can mimic it | The assistant's, at the owner's request of 2026-11-05 to characterize "what differentiates transient support that induces dependency and is hazardous to remove from transient support that builds new capabilities and is safe to remove", with reintroduction and ecological recovery proposed as cases.
